commit.message:
docs: generate the ipc api reference from the contracts (#1037)

* docs: generate the ipc api reference from the contracts

The hand-written docs/API.md documented three namespaces that do not exist
(agent, search, shortcuts) and omitted nine that do, while its header claimed
to be current.

scripts/gen-api-docs.mjs parses packages/shared/src/ipc/contracts with the
TypeScript compiler API and emits the whole page: every namespace, method
signature (verbatim source), TSDoc, channel constant and locally-declared
type. gen:api:check regenerates and diffs, wired into CI's lint-format job.

* docs: move the api reference's hand-written knowledge into contract tsdoc

The old docs/API.md held facts no signature carries: that `intent` picks a
provider's sampling numbers while `temperature` overrides it, that `embed`
chunks and mean-pools and retries a context overflow inside the same call,
that `aiGenerations.save` merge-upserts by jobUrl, that autopilot never
applies, that match is keyword-only unless asked. Each now lives on the
contract member it describes, so the generated page carries it and the code
owns it.

Deliberately not migrated: the enumerated board-id list (already stale
against BOARD_IDS — it missed jobicy) and the `ai:pull-progress` event name
(no such string in the repo). The pointers stay; the copies go.

* docs: point the ipc recipe at the generator instead of the generated page

CONTRIBUTING, the docs-standards skill and the project-steward agent all told
their reader to "document the new namespace in docs/API.md" — the one edit
that file now rejects. They say TSDoc on the contract member, then
`pnpm gen:api`.

* docs: stop the api generator inferring what an empty channel registry means

An empty `*_CHANNELS` const rendered as "this namespace exposes no invoke
channels", which is false: notifications has nine live commands and invokes
their Tauri names directly, as its own doc comment says. Report the
structural fact instead, and state the arithmetic when a registry covers
only some of a namespace's methods.

* docs: send rule 14 to the generator, not to the generated page

docs/API.md is now emitted from the ipc contracts and CI fails on drift, so
the recipe for a new capability has to say where the prose goes — TSDoc on the
contract method — or the next person hand-edits a generated file and loses the
edit on the next run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(gen-api): fail on duplicate exported names across contract files

The declaration and const maps are keyed by bare name across every contract
file, so a name exported twice silently overwrote the first entry and a
namespace could resolve to another file's interface — rendered under the wrong
heading, plausibly and wrongly. Fail instead of qualifying the key by file: a
real clash is a bug a human should see, not something for the generator to
paper over.

* fix(scripts): diff generated docs against the commit, not the index

`git diff --exit-code -- <file>` compares the working tree to the index, so a
regenerate-and-stage leaves a stale committed copy passing the freshness gate:
it only ever proved the worktree matches whatever was staged. Compare against
`HEAD` so the committed file is what gets checked.

`gen:workflows:check` had the identical hole — it is where the shape was copied
from — so both are fixed here rather than leaving a known-vacuous gate beside a
fixed one.

* fix(gen-api): anchor paths to the script, and keep failures path-free

CONTRACT_DIR, OUT_FILE and repoPath() all resolved against process.cwd(), so
running the generator from anywhere but the repo root read no contracts and
would have written docs/API.md outside the repo. Anchor to the script's own
location, the way packages/shared/scripts/gen-ipc-rust.ts already does.

fail() also escaped to Node's default handler, which prints a stack trace full
of absolute paths — the exact leak AGENTS.md rule 1 forbids. Catch at the top
level, print the message alone, exit non-zero; filesystem errors carry an
absolute path in the message itself, so the repo root is stripped from it too.

* fix(gen-api): escape backslashes before pipes in table cells

Cell escaping handled the pipe but not the backslash, so a backslash in front
of a pipe re-enabled the cell break and a literal escaped pipe in source prose
rendered as markup: the namespace row split into four cells instead of three.
Escape the backslash first, then the pipe, and collapse whatever whitespace the
paragraph fold left behind so a first-paragraph bullet list cannot end the row
either.

Reported by CodeQL (incomplete string escaping or encoding) and CodeRabbit on
the same line.

* fix(gen-api): resolve import specifiers against the files on disk

The referenced-types list rewrote a `.js` specifier to `.ts` and published
whatever came out. linkedin.ts imports './boards' with no extension, so the page
carried a link to a contracts path with no file behind it. Resolve the
specifier to a real file and fail when none matches, rather than emitting a
dead link.

Default and namespace imports were skipped by a bare `continue`, so their types
went undocumented with nothing to show anything had been dropped; both are now
hard errors, consistent with the rest of the generator.

* fix(gen-api): state the channel arithmetic only where it is true

The sentence fired on any inequality between channel keys and methods, but it
reads "registers N of this namespace's M methods". A `*_CHANNELS` const that
also carries event channel names makes N greater than M, and the page then
published a count larger than the total it was counting out of. Restrict it to
the direction it describes; a surplus is not a fact about the methods, so it is
left unstated rather than guessed at.

* docs: point the geocode tsdoc at the file that defines to_city_country

The reference named the geocoding directory, which does exist but holds the
offline geonames path; `to_city_country` is defined in the sibling
geocoding.rs. Name the file that contains the function, and regenerate.

* docs(gen-api): describe the freshness gate as it now runs

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
chore: update export benchmark data [skip ci]

fix: make in-flight backend work survive navigation, and stop logs leaking paths (#1036)

* test(scripts): make a stale subscription note fail the build

An audit of all nine route-scoped entries against the code found eight of the
nine notes wrong. Three described a loss that had already been fixed, four
understated what is lost, and one named a cause that is simply not what the
code does. Only the activity-feed note was accurate.

The notes rot because nothing couples them to the code they describe: #1019
fixed the jobs scrape and never touched the note beside it, and #1025 later
edited this very file without noticing that note was by then obsolete. The
guard enforced that a note EXISTS, never that it is true.

So each route-scoped entry now carries a short content hash of the file it
describes, and the check fails when the file drifts, printing the note so
re-reading it costs seconds. It over-fires by design: a formatting change also
trips it, and the fix is a one-line hash update. Always-mounted entries are
exempt because their note is a structural claim, not a description of loss.

Notes rewritten to lead with the observable symptom, and to say what is NOT
lost as well — several of these misled a reader precisely because they listed
only the loss and stayed silent about recovery that had since landed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(logging): stop leaking paths/urls/credentials via bare {e} in log macros

AGENTS.md's path-privacy rule bans absolute paths, usernames, and home dirs
from ever reaching a log line. ~100 non-scraping call sites did it anyway via
log::{warn,error,info,debug}!("...: {e}") where e wraps a rusqlite::Error
(InvalidPath embeds the DB path), a filesystem std::io::Error, or a
reqwest::Error (embeds the full request URL, sometimes with a credential in
the query string) - the shape applications::ApplicationStore::open already
documents the fix for.

Triage: fixed with .code() where the site is an exact match for that
documented precedent (a *Store::open failure), or with the more informative
observability::sanitize_reason(&e.to_string()) everywhere else, since it
keeps the safe part of the message instead of discarding it. 12 sites were
left as bare {e} with a stated reason (a pure parse/logic error that cannot
structurally carry a path/URL/host/credential, e.g. an in-memory PDF parse,
a fixed-template rate-limit message, or a reqwest error already stripped of
its URL upstream via .without_url()).

extension_bridge/mod.rs crossed the R8 hard LOC cap once its five fixes
expanded past one line each; split its token/opt-in persistence functions
into a new extension_bridge/persist.rs sibling module, mirroring the
autotrack.rs split already documented in that file.

scraping/** (45 sites, mostly reqwest/keyring errors) is scraping-applier's
domain, out of this pass's primary-path scope - tracked as debt in the
companion guard (scripts/check-log-error-leaks.mjs), not fixed here.

* test(logging): add a drift guard for the {e}-in-log-macro leak class

Fixing every known site is not durable on its own - #125 lands next week
without something that fails the build on a new one. Mirrors the house
scripts/check-*.mjs + .test.mjs shape (check-event-subscriptions.mjs's
declare-it-or-fail inventory in particular): every log::{warn,error,info,
debug}!(...{e}...) site in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src is either fixed (so it
no longer matches) or declared in ALLOWLIST with a one-line reason, tagged
safe (provably cannot leak) or debt (scraping/** sites left for that
domain's own author). Both directions are checked so the list cannot rot: an
undeclared site fails, and so does an ALLOWLIST entry whose site got fixed,
moved, or deleted without the entry being removed.

Mutation-tested by hand against the real repo before wiring it in: reintroduced
a leaking {e}, confirmed the guard goes red with the new site named; reverted,
confirmed green; separately fixed a debt site in place without touching its
ALLOWLIST entry and confirmed the guard goes red for the OTHER failure mode
(a stale entry), then reverted that too. A guard driven only off its own data
can't catch a deletion - ALLOWLIST is hand-written, not generated from the
scan it's checked against.

Wired into package.json (check:log-error-leaks), the CI lint-format job
(alongside toolchain-pin/event-subscriptions/adr-citations), and the
pre-push hook's RUST-gated section (pure text scan, no cargo needed, so it
runs before the cd into src-tauri).

* fix(jobs): persist scrape progress across a remount

useScrapeProgress resets to null on every mount and, on the default
single-board scrape, only ever fires once as the run ends -- so
navigating away and back showed a false 0% for the rest of the run.
job_progress already persists the same fraction into JobRecord, and
the watchdog already polls that record; feed it into a fallback used
whenever no live progress event has arrived this mount. Also give the
watchdog poll a leading call so the fallback lands immediately instead
of after the first 2.5s tick.

* fix(resume-pipeline): recover the failure reason after a remount

setError was live-listener-only, so a run that fails while the tailor
panel is unmounted (job.failed never reaches it) left the wizard with
no trace of what happened on remount. Fall back to the persisted
stoppedReason (via the existing stoppedSuffix mapping) when no live
error landed.

* fix(updater): stop check/download from discarding an in-flight update

updater_check unconditionally reset downloaded_bytes and swapped the
Update object, so a returning caller discarded a completed download
(forcing a full re-download) or raced one still in progress; report
back the known state instead. updater_download gets the same
re-entrancy guard job_start_exclusive already gives ai.reembed/
ai.indexStale, plus a Drop-based guard so a mid-transfer panic can't
leave the flag stuck.

ai_pull_model now uses job_start_exclusive so a second concurrent
pull of the same model re-attaches to the existing job id instead of
starting a fresh multi-GB download.

* fix(jobs): explain a scrape that fails off-page and refresh postings

The watchdog's failed/cancelled branches passed no summaries to
finishScrape, so a scrape that failed while the user was on another
route came back to an empty chip strip and no note -- the only copy of
the reason lived in scrapeOutcome, which renders solely inside the
drawer handleStartScrape already closed. Restore scrapeSummaries/
scrapeFailureNote on recovery, sanitizing the backend error the same
way the live job.failed event path already does (an unsanitized path
was landing straight in the UI). Also invalidate postings after a
completed recovery, matching the live event handler, so a 30s
staleTime can't leave the pre-scrape list on screen.

* fix(autopilot): close the run-status staleness hole and persist the error banner

useAutopilots inherited the 30s default staleTime with nothing invalidating
it when a run starts, so a remount inside that window could show idle with
an enabled Run button for a run still executing. Give it staleTime: 0.

Move the Run/Apply error banner from a useAutopilotRun-local useState into
the session store so it survives a navigate-away-and-back, matching the
persisted-badge cases and covering the concurrent-run refusal, which has
no other trace. Also corrects a comment that credited the terminal-step
invalidation with recovering a run that finished off-page, which it can't
(the subscription itself unsubscribes on unmount).

* fix(onboarding): reattach the ollama pull to a job already running

pullJobId lived only in useModelPull's own state, so any unmount of the
panel (tab switch, back/forward, or leaving the wizard) lost it forever
and no later job.stream/job.completed for the still-running pull could
match again -- the panel silently re-offered Download for work already
in flight.

On mount, re-read the job registry for an active ai.pull_model job and
resume tracking its id. ai_pull_model is exclusive, so at most one can
be running app-wide.

* fix(settings): stop the updater hook resetting to idle on remount

The settings panel's useUpdater() is one of three independent
instances (banner, menu, this panel), each with its own local status
and its own updater:status subscription. The banner/menu never
unmount so they never lose it, but this panel mounts/unmounts with
route navigation and had no way to learn the current status on
remount -- there is no backend command to ask for it, only the push
event -- so it rendered a stale idle, including a live "Check now"
button for an update already downloading or done.

Move status into a small synchronous external store shared by every
useUpdater() instance, so a remounted one immediately reads whatever
any other mounted instance already learned.

* docs(scripts): rewrite the subscription notes against the fixed code

The tripwire added earlier on this branch fired on its own merge, for four of
the six files these fixes touched. That is the mechanism working: each note
described a defect that no longer exists.

Rewritten to describe what the code does now, and to keep saying what is still
lost — the streamed resume draft, the autopilot step log, and a model pull that
reaches a terminal state inside the unmount/remount gap are all accepted
losses, not oversights, and a note that lists only the good news is how these
went stale the first time.

Records a blind spot the first real firing exposed: the hash covers the
declared file only, so a note also goes stale when the behaviour it describes
changes in something that file merely calls. Both misses came from this one
batch — JobsPage's note was fixed inside useScraping, update-section's inside
the updater service and its Rust command — and neither declared file was
touched, so neither tripped. Hashing the transitive import graph would fire on
nearly every commit and be ignored within a week, so the trade stands and the
two entries say in their own text that they were fixed elsewhere.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scraping): close the log-error-leak debt the fleet sweep skipped

The prior sweep (8a01a297) fixed ~100 non-scraping log::{warn,error,info,debug}!
sites that interpolated a caught error via bare {e} and left the 45 scraping/**
sites as tracked debt, guessing they were pattern-identical reqwest/keyring
leaks. Tracing each site's concrete type instead of pattern-matching the macro:

- 12 were genuine leaks and are now fixed with
  observability::sanitize_reason(&e.to_string()): 7 OS-keyring errors
  (Adzuna/JSearch/Jooble/Apify credential slots, Comeet company uid + token),
  a rusqlite execute() error clearing board_health on factory reset, cookie
  export/import filesystem paths (board_login/mod.rs + import.rs, both reading
  real browser-profile paths despite a "log without values" comment that the
  code didn't back up), and a genuine one: scraping/linkedin/api_client's page
  loop wraps reqwest::Error via error.rs's default From impl (no
  .without_url()), so a transport failure embedded the full LinkedIn search
  URL - including the user's free-text keywords/location - in the log.

- The remaining 33 were already safe and are now declared as such, not fixed:
  every named-board fetcher routes through scraping::http::fetch_text/
  fetch_json, whose transport-failure branch already strips the request URL
  via reqwest::Error::without_url() before wrapping in AppError::Network -
  the same protection net/http.rs's accumulate_capped applies fleet-wide - so
  the Adzuna/JSearch/Jooble/Apify API key living in that URL's query string
  never reaches these log lines even on failure. The rest are pure in-memory
  serde_json parse failures, an htmd conversion error, and a tokio JoinError -
  none of which can structurally carry a path/URL/host/credential.

scripts/check-log-error-leaks.mjs's ALLOWLIST now carries zero debt entries;
the two reclassification factories (httpChokepointSafe/inMemoryParseSafe)
document the shared reasoning once instead of 33 times.

* test(scraping): bound the transport-error leak test so it stops costing a minute

The new query-secret leak test dials port 9, the discard port. Unix refuses
that instantly; Windows lets the connect attempt sit until its own timeout, so
the test took over sixty seconds and every local `cargo test` run paid it.

`FetchOptions.timeout` already exists for exactly this kind of ceiling. Setting
it to 500ms does not weaken the assertion — a refused connection still fails
fast, a hung one now fails at 500ms, and both are the transport errors whose
`Display` must not carry the query string. Runtime went from over a minute to
half a second.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scripts): close the hashless route-scoped bypass in the subscription guard

A route-scoped SUBSCRIBERS entry with no hash skipped staleNoteEntries
forever, so its note could drift from the code with nothing to catch it.
violations() now rejects a route-scoped entry with a missing or malformed
hash before staleness is even computed; always-mounted entries stay exempt.

* fix(jobs): sanitize job_fail errors before they reach the tracker or ipc

job_fail/job_fail_with_data stored and emitted raw e.to_string() error
text, reaching the renderer through jobs_get, jobs_list, and the
job.failed event -- the same URL/path/hostname leak class PR #1036
closed for log:: call sites, on a different channel it never touched.

Route both through sanitize_reason at the single mutator boundary so
every existing and future caller is covered. The structured `data`
payload job_fail_with_data carries is left untouched -- only the
free-text `message` half is sanitized.

* fix(scripts): widen the log-error-leak scanner past literal {e}

The scanner only matched the literal `{e}` capture, so `{err}` (live at
postings/mod.rs:382 and platform/linux_appimage.rs:170) and a positional
"{}", e argument (live at autopilot_helpers/mod.rs:151) bypassed it and CI
entirely. findLeaks() now catches captured {e}/{err}/{error} and a bare
positional error-binding argument, bounded to the three names this crate
actually uses (measured against every log call site) so ordinary data
fields like {host}/{port} stay unflagged. All three newly-surfaced sites
were traced and declared safe with a one-line reason each.

* fix(documents): redact a posting id that embeds a full url before logging

CodeRabbit's premise ("PostingsCache uses normalized posting URLs as
IDs") is false for most boards -- greenhouse/lever/etc build an opaque
board:external-id -- but true for breezy/pinpoint/themuse, which build
JobPosting.id as format!("{BOARD_ID}:{url}"), embedding the posting's
full URL. That id reaches posting_vector_or_embed's failed-upsert log
line raw via match_resume's renderer-supplied job_id.

Redact job_id with the same shape-based redact_token classifier the
error already goes through, rather than hashing -- that would cost
every other board's debuggable id to close a leak only these three
have. match_resume.rs:217's "job not found in cache" error is left
alone: it echoes the caller's own job_id back to the same renderer
that supplied it (an established echo-point pattern elsewhere in this
command), so no new information is disclosed there.

* ci(windows): run the atomic file-replace test, not just cargo check

cargo-check-windows only ran cargo check --all-targets, so
std::fs::rename over an existing file (postings::InteractionStore
::save's write-then-rename) was never actually executed on this
platform -- rename-over-existing has different underlying semantics
per OS, and this repo has a recorded history of platform-exclusive
code compiling nowhere until release.

Add one narrowly-targeted cargo test for that single rename call, not
the whole suite -- keeps the job cheap (Windows runners bill at 2x)
while closing the specific gap.

* fix(extension-bridge): shape-constrain rejected origins before they hit the log

warn_rejected_origin_once logged the raw attacker-supplied Origin header at
all three of its call sites (PR #1036 sanitized log_handshake_failure's
e.to_string() in the same file but left these). sanitize_reason's
credential-token redaction is the wrong tool here: the origin is the one
diagnostic value a developer needs verbatim to add to extensionDevOrigins.

Add a narrow sanitize_log_origin helper instead: strip control characters
(newline/CR/ESC/NUL, the log-line-forgery and ANSI-escape shapes) and cap the
length, so the origin's content survives but its shape can't smuggle a
forged log line or flood the log.

* fix(extension-bridge): close the pairing token's brief world-readable window

persist_token wrote the token via std::fs::write then set_permissions(0o600)
afterward, so on unix the file briefly existed at the process umask between
the two calls -- group- or world-readable on a multi-user box. The
set_permissions failure was also swallowed with `let _ =`, so a box where it
fails silently kept a readable pairing secret.

Open the file with the 0o600 mode baked into the create syscall itself
(OpenOptions::mode) so a brand-new file is owner-only from its first byte on
disk, with no window. `.mode()` only applies on creation though, so keep the
trailing set_permissions call to self-heal a pre-existing wrong-permission
file (first-create and rotate both go through this one function); its
failure is now logged and propagated instead of discarded.

Mutation-checked in a standalone repro against the old two-step pattern:
both a final-mode assertion and a concurrent-poller race test (permissive
umask, 2M busy-poll iterations, 4 runs) could not distinguish old from new
in the success path -- the old code reaches the same end state and the
TOCTOU window is real but too short for a black-box test to observe. Noted
plainly in the test module rather than claiming coverage the tests don't
have.

* test(scraping): pin that every board runs through the http chokepoint

The log-leak allowlist declares autopilot_helpers' scrape-failure log safe, and
that reasoning runs three hops: the error comes from engine::run_boards, which
reaches every board through scraping::http::fetch_text/fetch_json, whose
transport-error branch already strips the url. The last hop holds only while no
board takes the Browser arm, and nothing enforced it.

So the first browser-mode scraper would have silently re-opened a url leak a
reviewer had already signed off as impossible, with no test anywhere to notice.
The assertion is on the registry rather than in the allowlist because that is
where the property actually lives.

Mutation-checked by inverting the predicate: the test fails and names all 24
boards.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(onboarding): settle a model pull whose terminal event raced its adoption

PR #1036 review finding: useJobEvents drops a job.completed/job.failed
that arrives before pullJobId commits (jobs.list is an IPC round trip),
and ai.pull_model fires that event exactly once. The reattach effect now
re-reads the job's own status right after adopting it and settles
immediately, instead of depending on catching the event at the right
moment. The commit into the ref backing that check is synchronous too:
an already-resolved promise can unwind entirely through microtasks
before a setState-triggered render ever gets a scheduler turn.

* test(scripts): flag a positionally-passed error.to_string() in the leak scanner

The scanner caught a bare positional `e` but not `e.to_string()` — the same
leak, one method call away from detection. `.to_owned()` has the same shape.

Measured before widening rather than after: there are currently ZERO such sites
in the crate. All 93 `.to_string()` occurrences near a log macro are the
sanctioned `sanitize_reason(&e.to_string())` wrapper. So this is a tripwire for
a shape nobody writes today, not a fix for a live leak, and the doc comment
says exactly that so a later reader does not infer a leak was found here.

The wrapper is excluded structurally, not by string matching: the whole
top-level argument is tested, and `sanitize_reason(&e.to_string())` is a
different call from `e.to_string()`. Pinned by its own test, because a pattern
that flagged the sanctioned fix would light up ~100 correct sites and turn the
guard into noise nobody reads.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): share updater download-progress metrics across instances

Only status moved to the module-level store; downloadSpeed/downloadedBytes/
totalBytes/timeRemaining stayed per-instance useState, so a remounted panel
showed the right label over a blank/zero progress readout for one tick.
Byte counts now derive straight off the shared status (downloading already
carries downloaded/total); speed/time-remaining move into the same shared
snapshot with their rate history, so a fresh mount sees the real numbers
immediately instead of restarting a blank history.

* docs(updater): stop asserting the banner never unmounts

The shared rate history is safe because a listener stays alive for the whole
download, and the comment justified that with "the banner never unmounts".
It nearly does: __root.tsx renders it inside ProtocolVersionGate, which swaps
in an ErrorState instead of children on a protocol mismatch, so every listener
can go away at once.

The consequence is bounded — one speed reading computed against a stale
timestamp after the gate reopens, then self-correcting — and only reachable
from a state where the app already shows a fatal error, so it is not worth
guarding. Recorded rather than fixed, because this same always-mounted
assumption has now been stated twice on this PR and was imprecise both times.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scraping): sanitize the autopilot board-failure log, drop the chokepoint proof

Round-2 review on #1036 found the chokepoint argument for autopilot_helpers/mod.rs:151's
log-error-leak exemption was unsound: it reasoned every board reaches the network
through scraping::http::fetch_text/fetch_json because every registered scraper reports
ScraperMode::Http, but that mode is declared transport, not enforced transport.
LinkedInScraper reports Http and still bypasses the chokepoint two ways: its
LinkedInHttpClient sends raw reqwest requests whose failures convert via the un-redacted
From<reqwest::Error> impl, and boards/linkedin/mod.rs's resolve_geo_id calls
net::http::shared() directly. Tracing it further: a first-page search failure surfaces
that raw AppError::Network(url) as BoardScrapeSummary.error, which used to reach this
log line as a bare positional {err} with nothing between it and the reader — a real leak
of the user's free-text search keywords/location, not a hypothetical one.

Removes the need for the argument instead of repairing it: sanitize_reason(err) at the
log site now redacts paths/URLs/hosts/credentials generically, regardless of which
transport produced the string, matching the identical pattern already used two lines
below (scrape_diagnostics) and by board_health's clean_error. The ALLOWLIST entry for
this site is dropped — the log call no longer interpolates a bare error identifier, so
the scanner no longer flags it at all.

Deletes every_board_runs_through_the_http_chokepoint (scraping/boards/mod.rs): it
asserted the declared ScraperMode, not the transport actually used, so it was coverage
theatre for the property that mattered. Nothing depends on "every board is Http"
anymore — the 24 httpChokepointSafe() allowlist entries were independently re-verified:
each is traced to scraping::boards/aggregator's own fetch_text/fetch_json call, none
sits on a LinkedIn path, so their soundness never rested on this test's property either.

Considered a mechanical guard scanning scraping/boards/**+scraping/linkedin/** for raw
reqwest::Client/.send() (mirroring check-log-error-leaks.mjs's shape). Viable, but not
built here: nothing currently depends on the invariant it would encode (LinkedIn's own
two log sites are already independently sanitized), and it would need real CI/pre-push
wiring plus a paired test file to be more than dead weight — out of proportion to this
review-round fix. Left as a follow-up candidate, not built as a silent no-op.

Mutation-checked by execution: reverting the sanitize_reason(err) call makes
check-log-error-leaks.mjs fail loudly on the undeclared site again; restoring makes it
pass. cargo fmt --check / clippy --all-features -D warnings / cargo test --lib
(4357 passed) all green.

* fix(jobs): key ai.pull_model's exclusivity on the model, not just the kind

Review finding on PR #1036: job_start_exclusive dedupes ai.pull_model by
KIND alone, so a pull of "qwen2.5" while "llama3" is downloading silently
joined the llama3 job and returned its id -- the renderer would then watch
(and eventually believe it finished) a download it never asked for, while
the requested model never started at all.

JobTracker::start_exclusive_keyed groups on (kind, key) instead, stamping
the key onto the new job's payload so it round-trips through jobs_list/
jobs_get. Same model still joins the running job (unchanged behaviour);
a different model is refused with AppError::Validation naming the model
actually in flight, rather than silently adopted -- two concurrent
multi-GB pulls would compete for the same bandwidth and disk anyway.
claim_embed_job/EMBED_JOB_KINDS keep using the untouched start_exclusive.

For the renderer's reattach effect in useModelPull.ts: it must match on
job.kind === 'ai.pull_model' AND job.payload?.model === selectedModel,
not kind alone, or a remount while a different model is pulling will
still adopt that job.

* fix(onboarding): stop the model-pull reconcile read re-adopting itself

PR #1036 review finding (MAJOR): the reconcile read's terminal branches
call resetTracking(), which clears pullJobId and re-triggers the reattach
effect. jobQueue's cached job-list snapshot has no reason to refetch on its
own, so it still reports the job as 'running' — the effect re-adopts it,
re-reads jobs.get, and fires the success/failure toast again, looping at
the rate of one redundant IPC round trip per cycle until an unrelated job
event happens to invalidate the cache.

Track already-settled job ids in a ref and exclude them from the adoption
predicate, so a stale snapshot can no longer re-adopt a job this hook
instance has already reconciled. finishOk/finishFailed now take the
settling job's id to record it. Tightened the two race tests from
toHaveBeenCalled() to toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) so a regression of this loop
fails them again.

* fix(onboarding): restore the mounted ref on effect setup, not cleanup only

PR #1036 review finding (MINOR): React StrictMode (the production app
renders inside it) double-invokes an effect in development - setup,
cleanup, setup - while preserving hook state between the two setups.
mountedRef was set true only from the initial useRef and back to false by
the cleanup, with nothing restoring it on the second setup, so after
StrictMode's dance it stayed permanently false and the reconcile read's
guard silently dropped every settle for the rest of the hook instance's
life.

Verified real double-invoke does NOT happen through renderHook's wrapper
option even when it renders a StrictMode element - only testing-library's
own reactStrictMode render option triggers it; the new test uses that
option, not a hand-rolled wrapper.

* test(onboarding): assert the live listener actually fired before trusting it

PR #1036 review finding (MINOR, but the important one): in both reconcile
race tests, handler stays null if jobs.onEvent is never called, so
handler?.(...) is a silent no-op - yet both tests still reached their
expected terminal state, because jobs.get alone (the reconcile path) is
enough to settle it regardless of whether the live event was ever
delivered. The tests were "passing" without pinning the ordering their
names describe: a broken or removed live-event subscription would not have
failed them.

Assert the listener was actually registered (jobs.onEvent called, handler
not null) before firing it in either test, so a regression there fails
loudly instead of silently degrading to the reconcile path alone.

* fix(onboarding): key the reattach adoption on model, not just job kind

Concurrent rust-backend-author fix: ai_pull_model's exclusivity moved from
job_start_exclusive (keyed on kind alone) to job_start_exclusive_keyed
(keyed on kind + model), stamping the model onto the job payload from
start. Two different models can now run concurrently, so this hook's
reattach effect - which previously matched any job.kind === 'ai.pull_model'
- would adopt a running pull of a DIFFERENT model than the one the panel
shows and render its progress under the wrong card. Refusing a second pull
at the command only guards a fresh handlePull call, not this registry scan.

Filter the adoption predicate on payload.model === selectedModel too, so a
job that fails the check is never adopted at all rather than adopted and
reconciled away.

* fix(jobs): replace start_exclusive_keyed's stringly result with an enum

R6 flagged Result<Option<String>, String> for a call that never fails: Err
carried the OTHER active model's name, not a diagnostic. KeyedExclusiveStart
(Started/Joined/Busy) says what it means at the call site and drops the
Result convention a reader had to know to decode it. Behaviour, the busy
message, and the payload shape ({"model": "<name>"}) are unchanged.

fix(scraping): wire the freehire params their spec never documented (#1035)

* feat(scraping): add per-request user-agent override to fetch_text

FetchOptions gains user_agent: Option<String>. None (every existing
call site) is byte-identical to today: fetch_text still writes
DEFAULT_UA. A board that wants to identify itself now has a real
override instead of the only prior option (putting user-agent in
opts.headers), which does not work: header() on RequestBuilder
appends rather than replaces, so a header entry would have ridden
alongside DEFAULT_UA as a second header line instead of overriding it.

Regression test proves the override REPLACES, not appends, by
inspecting the actual request wiremock received (not just a header()
matcher, which only proves the override value is present, not that
the default is absent). Mutation-checked by execution: reverted the
fetch_text line to the old unconditional DEFAULT_UA write, confirmed
the test goes red with the wrong value on the wire, restored.

* fix(scraping): wire freehire date filter and adopt issue #1026 spec fixes

freehire's own maintainer audited their published spec after PR #1008
and disclosed (issue #1026) that it had documented 17 of ~35 real
query parameters. Live-verified against the production API before
writing any of this down (spot-checked posted_within_days, reality,
meta.ignored_params, and the rate-limit headers against
https://freehire.me directly, 2026-08-18) rather than taken purely on
the maintainer's word.

- The real bug: date_filter reaches the wire. fetch_freehire took
  _date_filter: Option<&str> — accepted and thrown away, because the
  old spec had no date parameter. Maps our 9-token date_filter
  vocabulary onto posted_within_days (whole days, live-verified),
  reusing the SAME 3-day sub-day floor already established for
  adzuna_max_days_old/jsearch_date_posted rather than inventing a new
  number. None (no filter) omits the parameter entirely, since
  freehire's own "omit" semantics is genuinely unfiltered.

- Identifying User-Agent (freehire_user_agent, built on the prior
  commit's FetchOptions::user_agent): "ai-job-hunter/<crate version>
  (+https://github.com/saeedkolivand/ai-job-hunter-app)". Carries only
  the app name, the real crate version (env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")),
  and the public repo URL — no user data, no machine id, no locale.
  Not enforced or validated by freehire; buys advance notice before a
  field/limit changes instead of a 429 being the first sign.

- Rate limits: no new limiter code. The maintainer's disclosed budgets
  (600 req/min ordinary, 300 req/min for the agent search endpoint
  this module calls) are already handled by fetch_text's existing
  429/503 backoff, which already honors Retry-After — confirmed by
  reading scraping/http/mod.rs before writing anything, per the task
  brief. This tier's own traffic (one request per aggregator search,
  reached only after every keyed tier has failed or come back empty)
  sits nowhere near either ceiling.

- meta.ignored_params guard: freehire ignores an unknown parameter
  rather than rejecting it, so a typo returns the whole catalogue
  looking exactly like a legitimate broad result (live-verified: a
  country=gb typo returns 200 with
  meta.ignored_params:[{"param":"country","did_you_mean":"countries"}]
  and the FULL unfiltered set). fetch_freehire now checks
  resp.meta.ignored_params and returns Err — not the unfiltered
  data — when any of this module's own params are ever reported
  ignored, so a future upstream rename degrades this tier to
  Ok(empty) (the existing silent-degradation boundary) instead of
  shipping an unfiltered result set dressed as a filtered one.

- reality=fresh sent unconditionally, no user-facing toggle. Every
  other quality improvement this aggregator applies (sort_by=date on
  Adzuna/JSearch, dedupe_by_url everywhere) is likewise always-on with
  no settings knob anywhere in this board, so a bespoke toggle for
  just this one facet on just this one last-resort tier would be the
  odd one out. Live-verified to cut the unfiltered catalogue roughly
  in half (1,477,440 -> 662,112), which matters for a tier whose whole
  point is "enough to be useful without pulling a page nobody reads."

- Module doc rewritten to describe the API as it is now (documented
  rate limits + headers exist), not as a narration of the change.

Explicitly NOT adding cities: confirmed real, but geography (regions/
countries/cities) is a single OR-group on this API — countries=gb is
89,211 results, countries=gb&cities=London is 89,617 (WIDER, not
narrower, live-verified) — so adding it needs a location-UI decision
this change doesn't make. Left as a follow-up.

Every new guard mutation-checked by execution (deleted the feature,
ran, confirmed red, restored): the posted_within_days floor, the
identifying-UA wiring, the ignored_params guard, and reality=fresh
being unconditional.

chore: drop the 1.5 mb audit report from the tree, keep it in history (#1028)

* chore: drop the 1.5 mb audit report from the tree, keep it in history

AUDIT_REPORT.md was a 1.5 MB, 4272-line one-off snapshot: a full-history logic
audit scoped to every commit from the initial release through v0.123.0
(2026-07-07). It was never a living document, and 61% of its lines were the
requirements ledger and traceability matrix, two machine-generated tables
nobody reads twice.

Six weeks and roughly two hundred commits later, every one of its 141 findings
carries a `path:line` citation into a HEAD that no longer exists, so the most
likely way to use the file today is to be misled by it. Its top findings are
already closed: the privacy guarantee it called materially false is now the
enumerated third-party disclosure in README/SECURITY plus the machine-readable
inventory in tests/egress.rs and ADR-0005, and the orphaned support subtree it
found is gone, resolved by ADR-0006 to FAQ-only.

Nothing is lost. `git show cd1219ef7:AUDIT_REPORT.md` returns all 1,588,368
bytes, and that is now what the two ADRs citing it point at, with the caveat
that its line numbers belong to that commit rather than to HEAD.

Note for whoever next runs check:adr-citations: the report held 63 of the
repo's ADR citations, so the total drops 913 to 850 against a MIN_CITATIONS
floor of 800. The floor still holds, but the headroom is now 50 rather than
113. A future bulk deletion is likelier to trip it, and tripping it is the
guard working, not breaking.

* fix(hooks): stop the docs fast path prettier-checking deleted files

The docs/meta fast path piped `own_files` straight into prettier. That list is
a diff, so it names deletions too, and prettier exits non-zero on a path it
cannot open:

    [error] No files matching the pattern were found: "AUDIT_REPORT.md".
    husky - pre-push script failed (code 123)

So any commit that deleted a markdown file was unpushable, with an error that
points at the deleted file rather than at the hook. Found by deleting one.

Filters to paths that still exist. `xargs -r` because a deletions-only commit
would otherwise invoke prettier with no arguments, and bare `prettier --check`
walks the whole tree, turning a no-op into a slow full-repo check.

* fix(hooks): guard the empty doc list with a test, not gnu-only xargs -r

Review caught that `-r` is a GNU extension. BSD xargs, which is what macOS
ships, does not accept it, so the fix for the deleted-docs bug would itself
have broken the pre-push hook for every macOS contributor. Traded one platform
for another.

Builds the filtered list into a variable and tests it instead, which behaves
identically on both. The guard still matters: without it a deletions-only
commit runs bare `prettier --check`, which walks the entire tree rather than
doing nothing.

Verified against all three shapes: mixed existing/deleted checks only the
survivor, deletions-only skips prettier entirely, all-existing is unchanged.

* fix(hooks): stop a trailing deletion aborting the hook under set -e

Second review pass on my own fix, and it was right.

    existing_docs=$(... | while read f; do [ -e "$f" ] && printf ...; done)

The loop's exit status is its LAST iteration's. When the last changed doc is a
deletion, `[ -e "$f" ]` is false, `&&` short-circuits, the loop exits 1, the
command substitution exits 1, and `set -e` kills the hook right there. No
message, no gate, no push.

Reproduced before fixing. With a trailing deletion the script exits 1 and never
reaches the next line; with a trailing existing file it runs fine. That
ordering dependency is the only reason my own push worked and the bug shipped
looking verified.

`if`/`fi` exits 0 when the condition is false, so ordering stops mattering.
Verified across all four shapes under `set -e`: trailing deletion, trailing
existing file, all deletions, all existing.

Worth noting the shape, because it is the second time in two commits on this
same block: the failure is silent. The first version aborted with prettier
complaining about a file that was deleted on purpose; this one aborted with
nothing at all.

feat(scraping): remember which boards actually work between runs (#1027)

* feat(scraping): remember which boards actually work between runs

Every scrape already computed a per-board summary and then threw it away
everywhere except the last autopilot run, so a board broken since Tuesday
looked exactly like one that simply found nothing today.

Each run now folds its summaries into a new `scraping::board_health` store and
attaches the derived verdict to the summary the renderer already receives, so
the existing chips gain a second amber chip - "down for 4 runs, last worked 6
days ago" - beside the board's own result. Nothing is ever suppressed: a
failing board still runs on the next search.

The table holds exactly one row per board, upserted, so it is bounded by the
scraper registry rather than by time - there is no retention window to age out
and nothing to prune. A skip is kept structurally distinct from an error: a
board that was never contacted advances neither the verified timestamp nor the
failure streak, and does not clear an existing one. A cancelled run records
nothing at all, so a user's own cancel cannot manufacture a streak.

The correlation id is the scrape job id that already existed; none is minted.
The new summary field is serde-optional, so records persisted before this - and
every backup bundle carrying them - still deserialize.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(scraping): surface the remembered failure reason on the history chip

The store already kept why a board's current streak started failing, but
nothing read it back. The history chip now carries it as a native tooltip -
sanitized like every other persisted reason - so a board that was merely
skipped this run can still answer "why did this job source fail?" instead of
only saying how long it has been down.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(observability): move reason redaction down to the shared layer

`sanitize_reason`/`redact_token` scrub an upstream `e.to_string()` of paths,
URLs, host:port, emails and credential fragments before it is shown. They lived
in an L2 module, so an L1 store that needs to persist a reason could not reach
them and would have to rely on every current and future board keeping secrets
out of its error text - an invariant enforced nowhere.

Moved verbatim to `observability` (L0), which the layers that need it can all
reach downward. `commands::support` now imports from there instead of reaching
through the autopilot helpers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scraping): close five holes the reviews found in the board-health store

An unresolvable board id deliberately passes through to an ordinary error
summary rather than a skip, and that id arrives verbatim from the renderer, so
it was keying the PRIMARY KEY of a new on-disk store. `record_health` now
filters against the ids the RESOLVER recognised; the guard asserts the row
COUNT, not the absence of one id it happened to think of.

A recovery was only proved to clear the streak in memory. Every derivation test
lived on the pure fold and no test persisted a fail then a success for the same
board, so a `COALESCE` on the upsert survived the whole suite - and would have
resurfaced months later as "failing since" an outage long over.

`last_run_id` was stamped outside the fold, so a skipped run claimed authorship
of state it never produced - in exactly the broke-Tuesday-skipped-Thursday case
the module documents. It moves into the arms that actually contacted the board.

A board alternating pass and fail never badged: the streak resets on every good
run in between. Two lifetime tallies (appended as migration 2, never folded into
the first) answer "failed 6 of 12 runs" with no growth axis and nothing to
prune.

The stored reason is now redacted, not merely capped. This sink covers every
scrape including manual ones and is kept until the streak clears, so "the
autopilot store already persists the raw string" did not license it.

Also: a negative tally reads as zero rather than four billion, the stale
boundary is pinned on both sides, and the streak-window assertion is anchored so
it cannot pass on two Nones.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(autopilot): read board reliability live instead of freezing it into a run

The verdict rode on `BoardScrapeSummary`, which the autopilot store persists
verbatim as `lastRunSummaries` and `export()` writes straight into the backup
bundle. Importing that bundle on another machine replayed this machine's
failure streaks, error text and run ids as if that machine had lived them - the
exact outcome the store's own comment claimed to avoid by not being a
`DataStore`. It also went stale in place: an autopilot paused after a bad run
kept reporting a streak the store had since cleared.

Health is now stripped on the way to disk AND at the export boundary, and the
card asks `boards_health` for the current answer instead. That turns the
store's read API into a live query rather than dead code, and keeps the
verdict where it belongs - derived, never stored twice.

Adds the flapping badge, and fixes a double preposition in both locales
("not checked since 3 wk. ago" / "seit vor 3 Wochen nicht geprüft").

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scraping): bound board-health flaky tallies to a decayed window

verified_runs/failed_runs were LIFETIME counts, so a currently-working
board that had a 10-run outage kept reading unreliable for 31
consecutive flawless runs after recovery (clearing only at
verified_runs=41), while a board with a long clean history that
started genuinely flapping needed 100 more runs / 50 more failures
before the rate crossed the threshold at all.

decay_tallies() bounds both counters to a rolling window of
FLAKY_WINDOW_CAP (16) runs, halving them once verified_runs exceeds
it. failed is rescaled by the SAME ratio the halving applies to
verified, not halved independently — independent halving rounds
failed down less than an odd verified, which can inflate the ratio
and manufacture a Flaky verdict out of nothing but rounding
(measured: 17/4 = 23.5%, correctly not flaky, independently halves to
8/2 = 25.0%, now flaky, on a run that was a plain success).

Re-measured after the fix: the recovery scenario now clears in 16
flawless runs instead of 31; the alternating-failure scenario now
badges in 14 runs / 7 failures instead of 100/50. Decay is
forward-only (triggered inside fold on the next actual run), so no
migration is needed for rows already on disk.

Also narrows record_run to pub(crate) — the "bounded by the registry"
invariant depends on every caller pre-filtering to resolvable_boards,
which only ScraperEngine::record_health does — and documents the
undocumented `flaky` BoardHealthStatus variant on the TS contract.

* test(scraping): guard the positional health-zip against index drift

record_health re-attaches each board's health by zipping recorded
(the positions of resolvable boards within summaries) against the
store's returned results by POSITION, not by the results' own index.
The existing an_unresolvable_board_id_never_creates_a_health_row test
can't see a regression here: its only valid board sits at index 0, so
swapping the zip for health.into_iter().enumerate() produces identical
output either way.

Adds a discriminating case: a rejected id at index 0, followed by two
resolvable boards that both fail. Executed the mutation (zip ->
enumerate) locally — the new test goes red (the rejected id wears
fail-a's Failing verdict) while every pre-existing test, including the
one above, stays green.

* fix(translations): un-garble the never-worked-here chip's relative time

timeAgo() returns a relative phrase ("2 days ago", "yesterday"), so
the en neverWorkedSince key ("failing for {{since}}") composed to
"has never worked here · failing for 2 days ago" — and at the 1-day
boundary, "failing for yesterday". Reworded to "first failed
{{since}}", matching the de string ("gestort, erstmals {{since}}"),
which already reads correctly and needed no change.

BoardSummaryChips.test.tsx mocks t() down to a "key:opts" identity
stub, so it can never see the composed sentence. Added a focused test
that calls the real i18next instance (unmocked, same pattern
translations-parity.test.ts uses) with the real timeAgo output at both
the 1-day boundary and a multi-day case. Reverted the JSON key and
confirmed both assertions go red before restoring the fix.

* fix(jobs): refresh board health when a job event fires

keys.boards.health has staleTime: 10s and no refetchInterval, so a
mounted AutopilotCard only refreshed the reliability badge on window
focus/remount — right after a scrape or autopilot run finished
on-screen, the chip could still show the previous verdict.

useJobEvents is already the always-mounted subscription (via
useWorkerActivity -> StatusBar, per
scripts/check-event-subscriptions.mjs) that invalidates keys.jobs.all
on every event; it now also invalidates keys.boards.health there. It
fires for every job kind, not just scrape/autopilot ones, but the
health query is bounded by the board registry (cheap either way), so
filtering by kind isn't worth the complexity. No new subscribing file
was added, so check:event-subscriptions needed no new declaration.

Reverting the added invalidateQueries call reproduces the staleness
and fails the new test; restored.

* docs(scraping): fix a stale "lifetime" reference in is_flaky's doc comment

Missed in the decay_tallies commit — the rate is windowed now, not
lifetime.

* fix(scraping): rescale the decayed failure tally in u64, not u32

Found by the architecture audit of the decay commit, and it falsified that
commit's own doc comment.

`failed.saturating_mul(next_verified)` overflows u32 once the product passes
~4.29e9, and saturating_mul clamps BEFORE the divide. That destroys exactly the
proportionality the function exists to preserve: a board that failed 150_000 of
200_000 runs decayed to 2-in-12, read 16%, and came out HEALTHY. The doc
comment claimed the rescale handles an "arbitrarily large" legacy tally; it did
not.

Not reachable through fold today, which caps verified_runs at FLAKY_WINDOW_CAP
after every call, so the magnitude needed is ~131_072. It is reachable from a
hand-edited row, which is the same threat model this module already defends
against for a negative tally. Defending one sibling and not the other is how a
landmine outlives the person who knew about it.

The existing oversized-tally test could not catch this: it asserts only that
the cap is respected, and the cap IS respected while the ratio is being
destroyed. The new test anchors on an absolute floor instead — a board failing
three runs in four must not decay to something better than a coin flip. 75%
legitimately erodes to ~67% across the 14 halvings, because floor-scaling only
ever rounds down; 16% is the bug. Mutation-checked by execution: restoring the
u32 arithmetic reproduces 2/12 = 16% and the test goes red.

Also records what FLAKY_WINDOW_CAP does NOT say. It bounds RUNS, not time. At
the daily autopilot cadence that is one to two weeks, close to STALE_AFTER_MS;
for someone scraping manually several times an afternoon the same 16 runs span
hours, and the verdict forgets the morning by evening. That is the honest
behaviour of a counter with no clock, but nothing said so.

* fix(scraping): stop logging raw db-open/storage errors that can carry paths

board_health store open/record failures formatted the raw AppError, which
can embed the full data-dir path (rusqlite::Error::InvalidPath and similar).
Log the path-free AppError::code() instead, matching the existing learning
for database-open failures.

Grepped the crate for the same log::warn!/error!("...{e}") shape on an
AppError/rusqlite error: lib.rs has ~13 other pre-existing instances (dedup,
discovered, documents, ai_generations, applications, job_preferences,
contact_profile, ai_provider_config, referrals, spend, email_watch,
pipeline_cache stores) not touched by this PR — left as-is and reported to
the critic rather than widened here.

* fix(scraping): redact bare and multi-token credential shapes, not just assignments

is_credential only matched assignment shapes (key=, token=, "key":), so a
secret arriving as its own whitespace token survived redaction verbatim:
an Authorization: Bearer <token> header, a spaced token = <value>
assignment, or a bare sk-/ghp_-prefixed key with no marker around it at all.

- Add a prefix allowlist (CREDENTIAL_PREFIXES: sk-, ghp_/gho_/ghu_/ghs_/
  ghr_/github_pat_, akia) to redact_token's per-token classification, a
  structural check rather than an entropy heuristic (entropy scoring would
  flag ordinary hex/base64 ids like run/job ids just as readily).
- Extract redact_tokens(text), a multi-token scanner that additionally
  chains Authorization: Bearer|Basic <value> (gated on the Authorization:
  marker directly preceding the scheme word, so bare "Basic auth failed"
  prose survives) and a spaced marker = value assignment (gated on a
  literal = token immediately after the marker, so "auth token for board"
  prose survives).
- sanitize_reason and commands::support::redact_lines both now funnel
  through redact_tokens, so the support-bundle/crash-reporting path (ADR-027:
  the two consumers must not drift in redaction strength) gets the same
  protection as the board_health/autopilot path, not just a partial fix.

Mutation-checked by execution: reverting each new branch (prefix check,
Authorization/Bearer chain, spaced-assignment chain) individually turns the
corresponding new test red; restored after confirming.

* fix(autopilot): strip board-health verdict on import and on a cold load

export/record_run stripped the Track B1 board-health verdict from
last_run_summaries before persisting, but import() deserialized and saved
supplied summaries unchanged: a legacy backup (or a hand-edited bundle)
carrying lastRunSummaries[].health wrote machine-derived reliability state
straight back onto the importing machine.

Closed both directions with one shared strip_board_health() helper:
- import() strips before replace_all(), mirroring export()'s existing
  "belt and braces" strip.
- AutopilotStore::load() also strips on every cold parse of autopilots.json
  — the third sink: a file written by an intermediate build before these
  strips existed (or edited by hand) would otherwise keep re-persisting its
  stale health forever, since only record_run ever touches that field and

* fix(scraping): surface board-health reset/decode failures instead of swallowing them

clear_all() discarded its DELETE's Result with .ok() — Resettable::reset is
infallible by design, so a failed factory-reset delete had no way to surface
at all, leaving board_health.db intact while the reset reported success.
Now logs the error, matching PipelineRunStore::clear_all's existing pattern
for the same infallible-trait shape.

all() similarly discarded a per-row decode failure via
rows.filter_map(Result::ok) with no signal; a single corrupt row silently
dropped one board from every health read (indistinguishable from a healthy
board). Now counts dropped rows and warns once.

Neither gets a dedicated behavioral test: both are logging-only changes (the
happy path is unchanged and already covered by clear_all_wipes_every_board),
and the crate has no log-capture test harness to assert on the warn line
itself — consistent with the sibling PipelineRunStore::clear_all, which is
untested for the same reason.

Also pins record_run's current same-run-duplicate-board contract: it reads,
folds, and writes inside the per-summary loop within one transaction, so a
board id repeated in one record_run() call folds the second occurrence on
top of the first write (double-counts a single run). Unreachable from the
engine today (the caller dedupes boards first), but nothing in record_run
itself enforces that — the new test pins today's behavior so a future direct
caller, or a change that drops the engine's pre-dedupe, breaks loudly instead

fix(resume-pipeline): resolve a fabrication remove by its anchored line (#1029)

evidencePresent() decided isFabricationResolved/presentFabrication/
unresolvedCount by searching the whole document for the bare evidence
span, while removeEvidenceLines() deletes by exact line anchor. A
removed line whose bare span (a certification acronym, a date
fragment) legitimately recurs elsewhere left the entry stuck
unresolved forever, even though the flagged bullet was gone.

Mirror Rust's entry_resolved (report.rs): prefer the anchored `line` —
resolved once that exact text is no longer found anywhere in the
document — and fall back to the evidence-substring check only when an
entry carries no line (legacy reports). Deliberately does not AND the
two signals; that reintroduces the same bug (verified by mutation:
ANDing flips the new regression test back to red).

fix(landing): serve the /world clips from r2, which can send cors headers (#1032)

PR #1031 moved the clips to a GitHub release and broke the route. The release
URLs resolve fine to curl, which is how the check passed and why the break
shipped: curl sends no Origin, so it never exercises CORS at all.

scrub-engine loads each clip with `fetch(url).then(r => r.blob())` and hands the
blob to a video element. That is a cross-origin request, and GitHub release
downloads carry no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so every clip fetch threw and
the engine fell back to its poster stills. The page looked fine and had no
video.

R2 fixes the actual constraint rather than working around it: a bucket can
declare a CORS policy, so the response carries the header the engine needs.
Egress is unmetered there, so the Pages bandwidth ceiling that move was chasing
is gone rather than relocated. The objects went up with
`cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, which is honest because a
new clip set means new keys rather than mutated ones.

Verified against the live origin this time, not with curl: a real
`fetch().then(r => r.blob())` from the deployed site returns 200 and a
2,503,061-byte video/mp4 blob that produces a working object URL. Headers
checked directly too, and the allow-origin header is present for this origin
and absent for a disallowed one.

The tests now pin the HOST, not just the URL shape, because that is where the
defect lived: a same-origin `/world/vid/...` path and a GitHub release URL both
look correct and both break the route. Mutation-checked by execution against
each of those two states in turn; each turns three tests red.

localhost:3000 is on the bucket's CORS allowlist, so plain `next dev` works
without the NEXT_PUBLIC_WORLD_VIDEO_BASE override.

refactor(landing): serve the /world clips from a release, not from the repo (#1031)

33 files, 62 MB of video leave the tree for the `world-assets-v1` release. Two
separate problems, one move.

Git weight. Video does not delta-compress, so a re-encode writes every byte
again rather than a diff, and one re-encode round had already put roughly 38 MB
of unreclaimable history in the pack. Keeping the clips here meant every future
re-encode cost its full size forever.

Bandwidth. Sitting in apps/landing/public/ meant they were built into the Pages
site, so every view drew on the Pages 100 GB per month soft limit. At this
route's 20 MB device-set cap that is about 5,000 visits a month, which is low
enough to actually reach. Release assets are a different pool, documented with
no limit on size or bandwidth.

The poster stills stay, deliberately: about 2 MB, and they must paint before
anything is fetched. The published site drops from about 74 MB to 12 MB.

Every clip URL now goes through one `vid()` helper pinned to a release TAG.
Pinning is the point: publishing world-assets-v2 and bumping one line is atomic,
whereas mutating an existing release's assets would leave cached clients
disagreeing with fresh ones. `NEXT_PUBLIC_WORLD_VIDEO_BASE=/world/vid` restores
local files for offline work, and the directory is gitignored so a local copy
cannot be re-committed by accident.

The two tests that asserted every asset path starts with `/world/` split in
two, because that invariant now holds for the posters and not for the clips.
Both halves assert against LITERALS rather than against the config's own base,
so a regression cannot move the expectation along with the value; a fourth test
pins every clip to one tag so a partial bump cannot ship. Mutation-checked by
execution: pointing the base back at /world/vid turns two of them red.

The note claimed the session store keeps the stage but not the run handle, so a
remounted panel "can neither display nor cancel" the run. That stopped being

* docs(persistence): fix the subscription count, and stop citing adr-006 as the rule

Both from review, both correct, and both are the PR's own thesis turned back on
it: a stale record misdirects the next reader.

The subscription count was the half of the note I did not check. The rewrite
verified the reconnect claim against source and carried "FOUR subscriptions
(job events, notifications, pipeline stages, draft stream)" forward verbatim
from the old note. use-resume-pipeline-session mounts THREE: useJobEvents,
usePipelineStageEvents, usePipelineDraftStream. useNotificationEvents is neither
imported nor called; it appears once, inside a comment, as a stylistic
comparison. The fourth was presumably usePipelineRun, which is a useQuery with a

The ADR-006 citations pointed a reader at guidance that opposes the section

also makes this document's own "the streamed draft is legitimately transient
